paper_title: Thinking Slow, Fast Scaling Inference Compute with Distilled Reasoners
caption_used: Coverage as a function of the number of completions (k) for Llama-3B, Llama-3B + FT, Llama-1B, and Llama-1B + FT. All four models exhibit monotonically increasing coverage with additional completions on a logarithmic x-axis from 2^0 to 2^8. The 3B models begin at approximately 0.42 coverage and reach roughly 0.92 at k=256, while the 1B variants start near 0.22 and plateau at approximately 0.72 by k=128 with minimal further gains. Notably, fine-tuning provides a consistent advantage of approximately 5 percentage points for the 1B model throughout the scaling curve, whereas the 3B base and fine-tuned variants remain largely indistinguishable.
model_annotation: This plot illustrates the relationship between the number of completions and coverage for four different models: Llama-3B, Llama-3B + FT, Llama-1B, and Llama-1B + FT. The x-axis represents the number of completions, labeled as "Number of completions (k)", has a logarithmic scale, ranges from 2^0 to 2^8, and has tick labels at intervals of 1, showing values from 1 to 256. The y-axis is labeled "Coverage", has a linear scale, and ranges from 0.4 to 0.9 with tick labels at intervals of 0.1. The plot contains four lines: the Llama-3B line is blue and solid with circular markers, starting at approximately 0.42 and increasing to around 0.92 at k=256; the Llama-3B + FT line is also blue but dashed with circular markers, closely following the Llama-3B line; the Llama-1B line is light blue and solid with triangular markers, beginning near 0.22 and rising to about 0.72 by k=128 with minimal further gains; and the Llama-1B + FT line is light blue and dashed with triangular markers, showing a steady increase similar to Llama-1B but consistently higher by approximately 0.05 throughout.
